task.description:
WF-02, CODE-FIXER, small second fix round for REQ-104 after the second pass of both gates. Read handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-04c-security-reviewer.json (SECURITY-REVIEWER, PASS; its F1-F3) and handoffs/E2E104-20261103-01/step-04d-reviewer.json (REVIEWER, PASS; its L1-L4). Fix ONLY these:
1. SECURITY F1 = REVIEWER L3 (the one that matters): tools/test/e2e/kit/browser.js:202 passes the `env` option to noteBrowserForRunner (cleanup.js:99-101), so a spec calling withBrowser({env}) / launchBrowser({env}) is never registered with the runner and its Chrome survives a stopped hung spec. The registry location must come from the RUNNER's environment (process.env of the spec process, set by the runner) and not from the per-call `env` option; the per-call env stays what it was for Chrome's own environment. Prove it with a probe: a blocked spec that launches the browser with its own env object, SIGTERM to the runner, nothing left (count processes and folders before/after), and the same probe failing before the fix.
2. SECURITY F2 = REVIEWER L2: pass operator-controlled text (argv in the `command=` record line and runner.js:46-47, SAI_CHROME text in find-chrome.js:55,62) through safeText so a line cannot start with "::" and a 100 KB argument is cut. Keep the full list of "Places tried" in CHROME_NOT_FOUND (R-F1) readable.
3. REVIEWER L1: the two raw process.kill(-pgid, SIGKILL) calls in cleanup.js (about lines 153 and 203) use the shared signalGroup helper. SECURITY F3 (Info): refuse a pgid <= 1 in that helper (no kill of the runner's own group).
NOT to be done: REVIEWER L4 (copied helpers), SECURITY F4, unlimited frame size. Change nothing else; do not weaken anything; do not edit the six old guard tests or write kit tests (step 5); keep forbidden words out of tools/test/e2e. Format with `cd tools && npx prettier --write <your files>`; self-check `npm run format:check && npm run lint && npm run traces && npm run handoffs-check`; at most one full `npm test` (six guard tests red by design: HC-02, HC-03, HO-54, PK-7b, LP-3, CTL-13; name exactly which). Mac: one agent at a time; kill Chrome you start by process id; remove only your own temp folders; never rm inside the project. In result.changes every edit with the finding number; in result.issues what step 5 must test. Do not commit.
acceptance_criteria: SECURITY F1 fixed with a before/after probe

L4, F4 and the frame size were not touched, as ordered.

issues.text: WHAT STEP 5 MUST TEST for these fixes: (F1) a stand-in `ok` browser launched with an env option that lacks SAI_E2E_REGISTRY (and with one that carries a wrong value) while process.env of the spec has the variable -> a record <pgid>.json appears in the registry folder, and after a blocked spec plus SIGTERM to the runner no stand-in process and no sai-e2e-profile folder remain; with the variable absent from process.env, launchBrowser writes no record and does not fail. noteBrowserForRunner(pgid, profileDir) has no env parameter any more (it was not exported from index.js and no test or doc used it). (F2) runAll/parseSelection with an argument holding a newline and a leading `::` -> no stderr or stdout line starts with `::`, `\n` shown; a 100000-character argument -> output well under 1 KB; SAI_CHROME with newline/`::` and 100000 characters -> message cut and on one line; CHROME_NOT_FOUND from "nothing found" still lists all five places on separate lines. (F3/L1) signalGroup returns false and sends nothing for 0, 1, negative, fractional, NaN, a string; true for a live group; sweepBrowserRegistry still counts only killed groups; a record with pgid 0 or 1 is ignored; cleanupAllSync kills registered groups through signalGroup. Tests that check intentionally changed behaviour: none exists yet (the kit has no tests until step 5).

Same kind outside the order, NOT edited: browser.js START_FAILED messages (two places, `could not start "${found.path}"`) print the path of the SAI_CHROME program raw; the path must be an absolute path of an existing executable file, so a newline or a leading `::` is possible only in a file name made by the operator. Left for ORCH to decide (same class as F2, AP-014). Not done as ordered: L4 (copied helpers), F4 (frame size, SIGKILL of the runner O7).
